subject: Scaling commitment: blended uplift & co-term pathways for Cortex Health
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@cortexhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Capacity bump mid-term + co-term question

Hi Marissa,

Quick question on behalf of Cortex Health — our usage is ramping faster than forecast and we need to add ~1.5x GPU capacity starting June 1. We're currently mid-contract (ends 2028-01-15) and would prefer to co-term the new capacity to our existing renewal if possible.

Can you share: 1) a rough uplift % for adding capacity mid-contract (we'll do committed flat increase, not burst), 2) whether we can blend/annualize to co-term and how that affects the effective price, and 3) any one-time credits or pro-rata treatment you typically apply?

We'd like a ballpark this week to take to procurement.

Thanks,
Evan Park
Head of Cloud Ops
Cortex Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity bump mid-term + co-term question

Evan — thanks for the note and congrats on the accelerated uptake. High-level options (ballpark figures, subject to finance approval):

Option A — Immediate add-on (mid-contract uplift):
- 12% uplift on the unit price for the added capacity, billed pro-rata from the add date (no change to original term).
- Credit: existing unused monthly credits (if any) applied first; no separate one-time credit.
- Fastest to implement; preserves current renewal as-is.

Option B — Blended co-term (annualize and co-term to 2028-01-15):
- We annualize the new committed capacity across the remainder of the term and apply a blended rate.
- Typical blended uplift we can give at this scale: ~8% effective uplift (lower than Option A) plus a one-time invoice credit to offset transition friction.

Other notes: we can also do a hybrid (partial immediate + partial annualize) if you want a softer immediate bill. I've attached a quick calc workbook so you can see the math (CortexHealth-Initial-Calc.xlsx).

Next steps: I need alignment from finance/ops on the uplift % and any one-time credit. Rafael / Laura — can you weigh in on approval thresholds? Evan — if you can share expected start date (you mentioned June 1) and whether you need the extra capacity in all regions or just US, that helps the calc.

- Marissa
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T10:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity bump mid-term + co-term question

Marissa — thanks for the clear options. A couple quick internal asks before we provide firm pricing to Cortex:

1) Margin impact: need to see the blended gross margin on Option B (spread across remaining term). If the blended uplift reduces margin below 30% we need executive sign-off.
2) Credit policy: one-time credits > $2,500 must be approved by me or Laura. Anything > $10k needs CS/Legal sign-off too.

Evan — can you confirm the expected monthly $ spend increase (ballpark) so we can run the margin calc? Also confirm whether Cortex will accept an amendment (SOW) and DocuSign flow for co-term.

Rafael
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity bump mid-term + co-term question

Ok — given Cortex's growth trajectory and strategic fit, I'm comfortable approving a blended uplift up to 10% with a one-time credit not to exceed $5,000 to smooth the transition.

Ask Legal to prepare an amendment that:
- annualizes the added units across the remaining term,
- sets the blended rate at the approved uplift,
- includes a clause clarifying pro-rata billing and that existing discounts/credits apply first, and
- calls out the new renewal date (2028-01-15) as the co-term target.

Marissa — if they confirm a June 1 start and US-only capacity, go ahead and get finance to finalize the numbers.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@cortexhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T17:30:00Z
Subject: Final quote and amendment (Cortex Health)

Evan / team — attaching the amendment draft and the pricing sheet (CortexHealth-Amendment-Draft.pdf, pricing-sheet.csv). Summary of final economics per approved path (Option B — blended co-term, US-only, effective 2027-06-01):

- Added committed capacity: +150% of baseline (US region only)
- Blended uplift: 10% on unit price across the remainder of the term (represents a blended effective uplift vs. current pricing)
- One-time credit: $5,000 applied to the next invoice after amendment execution
- Pro-rated charge for June (partial month): $8,750 (calculated in pricing-sheet.csv)
- New total monthly commitment (post-blend): $95,250 (monthly billing starting July)

If that aligns, the amendment is ready for signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/CORTEX-5789-AMEND

Notes: we included a short renewal acceleration clause (30-day notice prior to renewal for capacity changes) as requested by Legal. If you'd like the partial immediate/hybrid option, we can push a slightly higher blended uplift (~11.5%).

Thanks — Vivek
Sr. Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
v.kulkarni@redwood.com

> — Evan
